chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mokattib, Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem, Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim Tataneh, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Saqr ibn Dolaf, who said: 'I heard my master, Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him), say:'

'Whoever has a need from God, the Mighty and Majestic, let him visit the grave of my grandfather, Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him), in Toos, while in a state of ritual bath (Ghusl). Let him pray two units of prayer at the position of his head, and ask God, the Exalted, for his need in his supplication (Qunut). Indeed, He will respond to him, provided he does not ask for something sinful or for cutting off ties of kinship. Indeed, the place of his grave is a spot from the meadows of Paradise. No believer visits it except that God, the Exalted, frees him from the Fire and admits him into the Abode of Permanence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward and method of visiting the shrine of Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (a.s.) in Toos?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual efficacy of Ziyarat al-Qubur, specifically linking ritual purity (Ghusl) and prayer at the head of the Imam to the fulfillment of needs. It underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory merit of the Imams, portraying the shrine in Toos as a 'spot from Paradise' that guarantees liberation from Hellfire for the believer, provided the supplication is not for a sin or severing kinship ties.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 66-32 Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mokattib, Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem, Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim Tataneh and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority his father, on the authority of al-Saqr ibn Dolaf, “I heard my master (the 10th Imam) Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) say,

‘Whenever one needs something from God, he should go on pilgrimage to my grandfather’s shrine (i.e. Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.)) in Toos after having taken the ritual bath (Ghusl). He should say two units of prayer at the position of his head, and ask for what he wants in the ‘Qunut (when he raises his hands up to pray to God). If what he is asking for is not a sin or cutting off ties with his relatives, then God will surely fulfill his needs. Indeed the place of the shrine is one of the palaces of Heaven. Whenever a believer visits it, God will free him from the Fire and let him enter the Eternal Abode.”
